cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Video games are an interactive media form where players actively participate in constructing the narrative and experience, unlike passive media forms.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Game genres: action, RPG, FPS, sports, puzzle, simulation, adventure, strategy, horror, MMO. Genres set player expectations and guide marketing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Platforms: console (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo), PC, mobile, and cloud gaming. Each platform has different conventions, audiences, and business models.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Industry structure: AAA (major studio) games have budgets of $100m+; indie games are made by small teams with limited budgets. The industry generates more revenue than film and music combined.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Representation in games: historically stereotyped (male heroes, sexualised female characters, underrepresented minorities). Recent games have diversified, but problems persist.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: PEGI (Pan European Game Information) classifies games by age rating (3, 7, 12, 16, 18) and content descriptors (violence, fear, drugs, bad language).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Interactivity is the key difference from other media forms — players make choices that affect the narrative, creating agency and personal investment.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Ludology vs narratology: should games be studied as games (systems, mechanics, rules) or as texts (stories, meanings, representations)? Both approaches are valuable.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Monetisation models: retail purchase, subscription (Xbox Game Pass), free-to-play with microtransactions, DLC (downloadable content), and season passes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Esports: competitive gaming has become a major industry with professional players, tournaments, and large audiences. Esports events are broadcast on streaming platforms.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Addiction and effects: concerns about gaming addiction (WHO recognises 'gaming disorder'), violence in games, and online harassment. Research evidence on effects is contested.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Video Games
cards.back: Fan culture: modding (modifying games), fan art, cosplay, and online communities extend engagement beyond playing. Game studios increasingly involve fans in development.

cards.front: What should you know about media studies exam tips — video games?
cards.back: 1. For Video Games, use media terminology precisely (e.g. connotation, denotation, representation, ideology) 2. Always analyse how media language creates meaning for specific audiences 3. Reference specific examples from set products to support your analysis 4. When evaluating Video Games, consider the role of media industries and cultural contexts 5. For extended answers, debate different interpretations before reaching your own
Evaluate how video games represent social groups. Refer to your CSPs. [12 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of video games, including key concepts, theories, and media contexts. AO2 (Analysis & Evaluation): Analyse and evaluate video games using relevant theories and frameworks. Consider different perspectives and reach reasoned conclusions.
